2608.04847.title: Do Language Models Know Their Slang? Queer Slang Understanding in User-Generated Content
2608.04847.paper_summary: Despite its cultural relevance and diffusion, queer slang remains underrepresented in Natural Language Processing research. Towards addressing this gap, we introduce Slang-Q, a manually curated dataset of naturally user-generated English sentences paired with queer slang terms and reference definitions, built upon a newly constructed taxonomy of 118 queer terms. We use this resource to conduct a first exploratory evaluation of language models on their ability to understand and define queer slang under varying prompting conditions. Slang-Q is intended as a basis for studying how current models handle sensitive, community-specific language and whether they can provide accurate and reliable information about such forms of identity and linguistic expression.
2608.04847.paper_summary_zh: 儘管其文化相關性和擴散，酷兒俚語在自然語言處理研究中仍然代表不足。為了解決這一差距，我們介紹了Slang-Q，一個手動策劃的數據集，包含自然用戶生成的英語句子，與酷兒俚語術語和參考定義配對，建立在新構建的118個酷兒術語的分類法之上。我們利用這個資源對語言模型進行首次探索性評估，檢視它們在不同提示條件下理解和定義酷兒俚語的能力。Slang-Q旨在作為研究當前模型如何處理敏感的社區特定語言的基礎，以及它們是否能提供有關此類身份和語言表達形式的準確和可靠的信息。
2608.04847.author: Arianna Denitto et.al.
